_docblock: PINNED NODE↔PLATFORM WIRE CONTRACT — v1 (EW-779, self-build finding OPS-21).
WHY THIS FILE IS LITERAL JSON AND NOT A TYPESCRIPT EXPORT.
The fleet builds the platform that dispatches the fleet. A regression in
/api/fleet/jobs/lease, the heartbeat DTO or the reconciler takes all six PCs
out at once, and the fix then has to travel develop → stage → main through
k8s-build (215-243 minutes, cancel-in-progress: false) on the machines that
just stopped. The conformance suite exists to catch that before a promotion.
A suite that imports the platform's own DTO classes and asserts they match
themselves proves NOTHING — it goes green on every change, including the ones
that brick the fleet. So the bodies below are hand-written literals of what a
DEPLOYED node actually sends and reads, transcribed from:
- apps/web/e2e/flow-fleet-enrollment-contract.spec.ts (the live-stack shapes)
- apps/node/src/core/fleet-client.ts  (selfDescription(), readNode, readString)
- apps/node/src/core/job-client.ts    (lease/heartbeat/complete bodies)
- apps/node/src/core/worker-loop.ts   (which FleetJobView fields are read)
They are NEVER derived from, generated by, or `satisfies`-checked against the
types under test, and this file is read with readFileSync — never imported —
so no TypeScript inference can quietly reconcile it with a changed DTO.
HOW TO CHANGE IT. Editing a shape here is editing the wire contract. Every
edit means: some deployed node no longer works, or a node built today cannot
talk to an older platform. Say which in the PR, and pin the old shape as a
`legacy` variant with an explicit `expect` rather than deleting it.
Directions the suite reports:
platform-too-new — the platform now requires something a deployed node
cannot send. This is the fleet-wide brick.
node-too-old     — a deployed node sends a field the platform now forbids
(whitelist + forbidNonWhitelisted makes that a 400).

current.note: What a node on today's build sends (all six self-description fields).

legacy.note: Pre-EW-777 / pre-cliVersion node. MUST stay accepted: a deployed node that cannot be upgraded first has to enroll.

minimal.note: Token only — the enroll-replay probe in apps/web/e2e/flow-fleet-enrollment-contract.spec.ts.

current.note: Slice T / EW-777 shape — modelIdentity present.

legacy.note: Pre-EW-777 beat. MUST stay accepted — this is the shape every not-yet-upgraded machine in the fleet is sending right now.

credentialOnly.note: A beat carrying nothing but the credential. An absent telemetry field means leave the stored reading alone, so this must never be a 400.

nodeIgnoresResponseFields.note: ASYMMETRY, pinned deliberately. FleetClient.heartbeat SYNTHESISES { ok: true, node } from readNode() and never reads `ok` — unlike FleetJobClient.heartbeat, which does check payload?.ok. Dropping `ok` here would pass unnoticed on the node and break the desktop shell and apps/web. Keep emitting it.
FleetClient.unenroll discards the body entirely; only the 2xx matters. Pinned so nobody assumes the node would notice a shape change here.

legacy.note: Credential-only poll. job-client.ts builds the body key-by-key and omits every unset option, so this is the shape an idle node sends.

nodeReadsResponseFields.note: MUST be >= 1 and MUST be present. The heartbeat and complete DTOs require it (EW-792), and leaseGenerationOf() drops anything below 1 — so a lease that omits it, or emits 0, costs the node its whole attempt. toJobView emits `job.leaseGeneration ?? 0`: a row backfilled by the migration therefore carries 0 and is guaranteed one lost attempt. Pinned so nobody 'tidies' the field away.

unreadResponseFields.note: status, targetNodeId, requiredCapabilities, attempts, maxAttempts, createdAt, startedAt, completedAt, queuedAt, queuedReason and cancelRequestedAt are emitted but not read by today's worker. They are pinned as PRESENT, not as read — dropping one breaks the Fleet UI, not the node.

legacy.note: A node that leased from a pre-EW-792 API receives no leaseGeneration in the view, leaseGenerationOf() returns undefined, and job-client.ts then OMITS the key — so it is 400'd on every beat and retries forever. This is a KNOWN one-way break, accepted deliberately (relaxing the DTO would defeat isCurrentLeaseGeneration's fail-closed check on 0). It is pinned as an expected, direction-labelled rejection so it is documented rather than hidden — and so a SECOND field made required this way shows up as a new failure.

currentFailure.note: job-client.ts sends `error` only on failure and `result` only on success — never both.

legacy.note: Same known EW-792 one-way break as the job heartbeat above. Pinned, not fixed.

nodeReadsResponseFields.reader: job-client.ts Boolean(payload?.ok) is the whole return value

selfDescription.note: Set equality across three places. A field added to the DTO but forgotten in the controller's explicit mapping, or in the node's selfDescription() projection, is computed, logged and then silently never stored — exactly how cliVersion and diskFreeBytes were first wired at the probe end only.

platformStatusCodes.note: Every code a node branches on. Changing one is a wire-contract change even when no field moves.

fleetDisabled.note: Deliberately 404, not 403 — a disabled deployment must look like a route that was never mounted. The node has no 404 branch, so it collapses this to `invalid-request`: indistinguishable from a typo in the API URL. Documented in docs/runbooks/FLEET_BREAK_GLASS.md rather than changed.

nonUuidJobId.note: ParseUUIDPipe rejects before any handler runs.

nodeStatusBranches.note: status → FleetClientError kind. Two DIFFERENT tables: the job channel has a 409 branch and the enroll/heartbeat channel does not.

killSwitch.note: Slice V / EW-778. The global stop flag is consulted inside lease, AFTER auth and BEFORE anything is claimed, and answers with an EMPTY LIST — not a 401, not a 403, not a 503. A 401 here would be read by every node as a revoked credential (job-client.ts maps lease-401 to `unauthorized`, which heartbeat.ts makes sticky and operator-visible), turning a reversible stop into a fleet-wide re-enrollment.
killSwitch.ungatedReason: A stopped fleet must still settle the work it already holds, or a cancel-in-flight could never resolve.
